translations./materials/0/description: Dry concrete with baseline traction—the simulation’s 1.0 reference.
translations./materials/1/description: Loose gravel reduces traction to 80% and adds noticeable rolling resistance.
translations./materials/2/description: Loose fine sand lets tires dig in and has the highest rolling resistance.
translations./materials/3/description: A shallow water layer leaves 35% of baseline traction, especially punishing for efficiency tires.
translations./materials/4/description: Saturated soil reduces traction and adds rolling resistance. Heavier payloads demand more torque and more careful routing.
translations./materials/5/description: Dark, coarse emergency-road pavement with credible wet traction and clear LiDAR returns.
translations./materials/6/description: Coarse drained grating preserves more wet traction, with higher drag and vibration than smooth plate.
translations./materials/7/description: A stiff, low-loss metal surface whose joints transmit sharp impacts; wet steel offers limited adhesion.
